description:
## Summary

submit delivers a change-proposal through Radicle's native patch flow: the artifact binds the patch identity in its handle, and each immutable submission round (version) binds the specific patch revision it delivered, so review and land bind to (patch, revision) — never to a mutable branch tip. Revision rounds publish as new immutable patch revisions. This replaces `deliver-change-proposal`.

Part of: #538.

## Scope

- `protocols/submit` and `workflow-contracts/submit.toml`
- change-proposal version-to-revision binding semantics (schema envelope)
- Submission/revision mechanics; tests and fixtures

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A prepared commit is delivered as a native Radicle patch with deterministic titling; the change-proposal handle carries the patch identity per the Groundwork identity grammar.
- [ ] Each delivered version records the revision it delivered; a revision round publishes a new immutable patch revision bound to the next version; previously delivered versions remain immutable.
- [ ] `submit.toml` names only manifest-registered mechanics — no forge operations; delivery and revision are verified by durable patch read-back.
- [ ] Tests and fixtures cover first delivery, a revision round, and verification failure paths; the protocol rendering documents the native patch flow where the submitting agent first meets it.

## Contract inputs

- **Behavior:** a delivered version resolves to exactly one immutable patch revision; review of that version can name it unambiguously.
- **Documentation:** the submit protocol rendering carries the patch-flow semantics standalone.
- **Code quality:** Traceability — version → revision → commit is one unbroken chain (`~/.groundwork/principles/`).

## Dependencies

Depends on: #598, #600.
title: task(submit): change-proposals delivered as native Radicle patches — versions bind immutable revisions
